title: Rewire Your Anxious Brain: How to Use the Neuroscience of Fear to End Anxiety, Panic, and Worry
author: Catherine M. Pittman, PhD & Elizabeth M. Karle, MLIS
target_audience: Adults experiencing anxiety, fear, or panic
Individuals seeking to understand and manage their own anxious thoughts or behaviors
Mental health professionals looking for neuroscience-informed techniques
Readers interested in brain science and psychological self-improvement
core_themes: The neuroscience behind anxiety and fear
The roles of the amygdala and cortex in anxious reactions
Differentiating between automatic (emotional) and cognitive anxiety
Practical strategies to 'rewire' the brain and change anxiety responses
Empowering individuals to regain control over anxiety
primary_purpose: To help readers understand the brain-based mechanisms that drive anxiety and to provide practical, science-backed strategies for reducing anxiety, ending panic, and managing worry effectively.

structure_format.narrative_style: Accessible, educational, and practical; explains complex neuroscience in layperson’s terms combined with actionable advice
structure_format.organization: Divided into two main sections: part one covers the science of anxiety (focusing on the amygdala and cortex); part two offers step-by-step techniques for managing both types of anxiety, along with exercises and real-life case studies
features: Step-by-step exercises rooted in cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) and mindfulness
Examples and case studies to personalize concepts

key_concepts_lessons: Anxiety arises from distinct but overlapping brain pathways: the amygdala (fast, automatic, emotional) and the cortex (slower, thought-based).
Understanding which part of the brain is driving one’s anxiety leads to more effective self-help techniques.
Cortex-driven anxiety can be managed by challenging unhelpful thoughts and redirecting attention.
Amygdala-based anxiety requires habituation and gradual exposure to reduce sensitivity.
Neuroplasticity means the brain can be 'rewired' through repeated practice of new thinking patterns and behaviors.
Self-compassion and consistent practice are imperative to long-term change.
notable_features: Focuses on the neuroscience of anxiety, making complex concepts accessible to lay readers
Provides both theoretical understanding and practical tools
Integrates case studies and real-life stories for relevance
Distinguishes strategies for amygdala-driven vs. cortex-driven anxiety
cultural_historical_context: The book reflects the growing public interest in brain science and the increasing mainstream acceptance of neuroscience as a basis for practical mental health tools. Published in the wake of expanded public dialogue around anxiety and mental wellness in the 2010s.
reception_impact: Praised for demystifying the biological underpinnings of anxiety
Widely recommended by therapists, counselors, and mental health bloggers
Lauded for practical, actionable advice and relatable case studies
Some readers suggested repetition in exposition, but most found its clarity and empowerment valuable
comparable_titles: The Anxiety and Phobia Workbook by Edmund J. Bourne
The Neuroscience of Anxiety: New Skills for Navigating Uncertainty by Dr. Bret A. Moore
The Anxiety Toolkit by Dr. Alice Boyes
